## Research Interests

<div class="research-summary">

### Galactic cosmic rays & propagation

- Transport of cosmic rays in the Milky Way  
- Diffusion, reacceleration, and energy losses in different ISM phases  
- Links between cosmic rays, gamma-ray emission, and radio observations  

### Astroparticle methods

- Bayesian inference for propagation and source parameters  
- Forward modelling with CRPropa-based simulations  
- Statistical treatment of multi-messenger datasets  

### Related interests

- Structure and turbulence of the interstellar medium  
- High-energy processes near shocks and compact objects  

</div>

## Current Work in Progress

<div class="research-current">

- **Bayesian modeling of Galactic cosmic-ray propagation**  
  Developing a Bayesian framework (with CRPropa simulations) to constrain
  propagation parameters using current cosmic-ray measurements.

- **Weak-shock reacceleration and the all-electron spectrum**  
  Studying how weak shocks in the ISM reaccelerate electrons / positrons
  and how this affects the observed all-electron spectrum.

- **Future directions**  
  Extending these models to include spatially varying diffusion and
  comparing with gamma-ray observations of nearby regions.

</div>
